newsitem.title: FRANCE: French shares close 0.6 percent higher.
newsitem.headline: French shares close 0.6 percent higher.

text.p: French shares closed 0.6 percent higher on Friday after a lacklustre and mixed day, dealers said.

The market had started with gains after having been closed on Thursday, ignoring Wall Street's overnight fall. It cut its gains ahead of the publication of weaker-than-expected April U.S. jobs creation data, spiked up after the numbers but the rally ran quickly out of steam.

The figures showed the economy was growing but not as quickly as economist believed, easing some fears ovr inflation and the need for a rate rise. The Federal Reserve Board's policy making FOMC council meets on May 20.
Wall Street's higher opening late in the afternoon lifted French shares again but in the end it closed below the day's high of 2,662.26 for the CAC-40 index.

The blue-chip index closed up 0.60 percent, or 15.84 points at 2655.31. The May future was down 0.19 percent at 2636.0 after close. Volume was five billion francs including 3.6 billion in CAC-40 shares.
On the political front, the Socialist Party published its election manifesto which contained few surprises.
The party wants to create jobs, has a "Yes, but" attitude to European Monetary Union, and wants to reform payroll charges to cut the cost of labour.

Socialist Party policy maker Dominique Strauss-Kahn told Reuters a parity of one euro for one dollar would be good for the economy and he said there had to be political talks if France would not meet the target three percent budget deficit of GDP.
Union Industrielle de Credit was the biggest loser with a 22.12 percent fall to 25 francs. The GAN unit requoted after a suspension since February 26.
Bull, down 4.90 percent at 47.50 francs, requoted for the first time since April 11 after the government sold 17.1 million shares. The share was suspended twice, once limit-up and once limit-down.
Rhone-Poulenc, up 1.38 percent at 199 francs, continued Wednesday's 4.5 percent rise booked on the back of 6.5 percent higher first quarter earnings.
